candidates.statement: In general, FDA’s guidance documents do not establish legally enforceable responsibilities. 27 Instead, guidances describe the Agency’s current thinking on a topic and should be viewed only 28 as recommendations, unless specific regulatory or statutory requirements are cited. The use of 29 the word should in Agency guidances means that something is suggested or recommended, but 30 not required. 31
candidates.context: This guidance provides information on how a person can submit a proposed draft guidance 16 relating to patient experience data for consideration by FDA. This guidance is intended to assist 17 stakeholders seeking to develop and submit such proposed draft guidance to the Agency. In 18 addition, FDA recognizes that stakeholders may have other information on patient experience 19 data that they would like to share with FDA outside of the guidance process and thus provides 20 information on other ways stakeholders can advance drug development by sharing patient 21 experience data. Section 3002(c)(5) of the 21 st Century Cures Act (Cures Act) directs FDA to 22 issue guidance on how a person seeking to develop and submit a proposed draft guidance 23 relating to patient experience data for consideration by FDA may submit such proposed draft 24 guidance to the Agency. 2

candidates.statement: As medical product development moves into premarket review and then the postmarket setting, it 71 may be informative to collect patient input on benefits and risks and better understand attitudes 72 toward or tolerance of potential medical product risks and how therapy side effects vary by 73 subpopulation. candidates.context: Patient perspectives on clinical endpoints in clinical trials and clinical outcomes can inform 61 stages of development from discovery through premarket review. candidates.statement: Stakeholders are not required to communicate with FDA in advance of submitting a proposed 201 draft guidance. However, when developing proposed content for disease- and indication-specific 202 recommendations for FDA’s consideration, it may be helpful (for FDA awareness) to provide 203 FDA with a brief summary of the expected content, along with a projected timeframe for 204 submission and a point of contact for potential follow-up. Ideally, these summaries will be brief 205 (2-3 pages at maximum) and should be sent only to PED- 206

candidates.statement: Under FDA’s Good Guidance Practice regulations, stakeholders can provide comments on a 299 guidance document at any time. They may also suggest that FDA revise or withdraw an existing 300 guidance document. 13 The suggestion should address why the guidance document should be 301 revised or withdrawn and, if applicable, how it should be revised. The suggestion should be 302 submitted as a comment to the public docket assigned to that specific guidance. To find an 303 assigned public docket, please visit www.regulations.gov and search for the specific guidance. 304
